title: Enums and matching
summary: An enum lists the shapes a value can take; match takes it apart.

blocks.html:
So far every value we built had one shape: a struct with a fixed set of fields. An enum is the other way to build a type. It lists the shapes a value may take, and a value of that type is exactly one of them.

Start with the plain case: names, with no data attached.

blocks.title: an enum of names

blocks.html:
Direction is a type now, and Direction::North is one of its four values: the enum name, two colons, the variant. Because the compiler knows the whole list, a match that forgets a variant is not a warning. It is a build failure.

A match is not a menu of suggestions. Take the program above, drop the last two arms, and you have a shorter match that looks perfectly innocent:

match heading {
Direction::North => println!("going up"),
Direction::South => println!("going down"),
}

The compiler does not shrug at the missing arms. It counts the variants for you and names what you skipped.

The build stops with:

error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `Direction::East` and `Direction::West` not covered
10 | match heading {
| ^^^^^^^ patterns `Direction::East` and `Direction::West` not covered

Under that it prints note: `Direction` defined here with the unhandled variants underlined, and suggests an arm you could add. That strictness is the feature: add a fifth variant next month and every match over the enum stops compiling until you decide what it should do.

blocks.title: variants that carry data

blocks.html:
Notice what we did not need: one struct per shape, a kind field to say which fields are meaningful, or a way to build a circle without a radius. The variants carry different data, and match is how you reach it. Each arm names a shape and unpacks its fields in the same line.

Patterns are not limited to whole variants. You can match literal values, ranges, and finish with a catch-all.

blocks.title: literals, ranges, a catch-all, and _
blocks.output:
something else: 7
seven, whatever the flag is

blocks.html:
This is the enum you will use every day. Code that looks something up may find nothing, and most languages answer with null, which fits every type and belongs to none. Rust puts the gamble in the type. The standard library defines it roughly as:

enum Option<T> { Some(T), None }

None is an ordinary value of type Option<T>, so getting the number out of an Option<i32> takes a match, and you must say what happens when it is empty. Rust has no null.

if let tests one variant and skips the rest, while let loops while the pattern matches, and unwrap_or(fallback) collapses an Option to a plain value: the number if there is one, the fallback otherwise.

blocks.title: Option<i32>: a box that holds a number, or nothing
match and if let on Option
blocks.output:
age is 30
still no age recorded
default to 0

blocks.title: while let keeps going while there is something
blocks.output:
working on 3
working on 2
working on 1
nothing left

quiz.q: What does the compiler do when a match leaves out a variant of the enum?
options: Refuses to compile and names the missing variants
Compiles, and panics at runtime if that variant turns up
Compiles, and the missing variants do nothing
quiz.why: Matching is exhaustive: every variant needs an arm, or a catch-all that covers what is left. The error is E0004 and it lists the variants you forgot.

quiz.q: Which value can a variable of type Option<i32> hold?
quiz.why: Option is an enum with exactly two variants: Some carries one value, None carries nothing. There is no third state and no null.

quiz.q: let maybe: Option<i32> = None; — which line prints a number instead of panicking?
quiz.why: unwrap_or takes the value when there is one and falls back to the argument when the Option is None. Option does not implement Display, and it has no positional field to index.

exercise.brief: The starter defines an enum for a traffic light holding Yellow. Write a match with one arm per variant and print exactly wait.
exercise.hint: Each arm is Pattern => expression, and the arms are separated by commas. You need three arms, one for Light::Red, Light::Yellow and Light::Green, even though only one of them runs.
